title: Telling the Ink Spots show tour again
summary: He repeats the 29-theatre tour with Cootie, the Ink Spots, Ella and Vinson, the Regal Theatre blizzard and empty Omaha.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, when you were with Cootie's band...

Yeah, when I was with Cootie's band, we had a show composed of the Ink Spots, Ella Fitzgerald, Eddie Vinson, Ralph Brown, dancers. They had quite a show. And we had theatres booked up in 29 weeks. No, sorry. We had a lot of theatres booked up across the country. Which they broke records in 28 theatres. We had 29 theatres booked up, and they broke records in 28 theatres.

And one day in Chicago, at the Regal Theatre in Chicago, which seats about five or six thousand people, maybe more than that, a big theatre... And they had people... It was a blizzard outside, and if you ever was in Chicago in a blizzard, you know they have some snow out there -- and some wind. They had people lined up four deep all the way around the block. You know, a Chicago block is a long thing. It's almost equal to five blocks in New York. And they had people lined up four lines deep to see the show. And we did about six shows that day.
It was a terrific drawing attraction. And that went on all across the country, from New York right into Los Angeles, San Francisco -- all the theatres was lined up around the block with people.

Only one theatre they didn't break the record in. That was Omaha, Nebraska. It was fifteen below zero there, and them people there didn't care who was in town. They wouldn't care if it was P.T. Barnum himself there. They wouldn't come out no fifteen below zero to see nothin'! You could throw a baseball in the theatre and wouldn't hit anybody, and nearly a whole week nobody showed up, except the shows. Heh-heh.
